Prepared by the Staff Communications Group

Buildings and Design
The Firm That Chose to Keep
By Philip Grierson, Architecture Correspondent
When the city looked for a firm to reopen the Ravensworth Building, a 1911 structure that had stood empty for fourteen years, Tolliver Architects was already known for restoring a small chapel nearby. The firm won the job because its plan alone kept the front of the building as it stood. --[1]--.
The same care for the old building guided the work inside. The building's previous owner, a fabric merchant, had left the interior in place. --[2]--. Its original staircase and light fixtures were taken out and cleaned on the premises. These pieces were later reinstalled one floor above their original position.
"A building of this age never gives up all its secrets at once," says Naomi Wickham, the lead designer. --[3]--. Halfway through the work, the team found a sealed doorway behind a plaster wall and chose to repair and reopen it. Three panels missing from that doorway were the only pieces newly made for the project.
Today five businesses share the building's four floors. A café and a bookstore fill the ground floor, while the upper floors hold a publishing office and two design studios. --[4]--. The project has also been named a finalist for a national restoration award.
Members of the public may visit the building on Saturdays and Sundays from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., although booking is required. Groups of more than ten may request a guided tour by writing to
[email protected]
.
From the March issue of Belvedere Monthly.

Copying and Printing

For many years our photocopying was sent to an outside supplier, which meant a wait of several days and a separate invoice each time. From this month the work is handled entirely within our own offices, and clients may order copies directly from us. Clients using the new in-house service can expect the following:

1. Our own staff run the copiers on site throughout our opening hours, so nothing you send us ever leaves the building.

2. You can follow the progress of every job from start to finish through your personal online account.

3. Finished copies are ready for pickup at our front counter on the same day they are ordered.

4. The account holder and anyone else named on the order may pick up completed work.

Two service levels are offered: Standard handling at $12 per order and Priority handling, for urgent work, at $30 per order. A minimum charge of $6 applies to any order of fewer than ten items. Account holders also pay a reduced binding charge of $4 when binding is added to any order.

To place an order, sign in to your account or call the order desk at 555-0192 between 8:30 A.M. and 6:00 P.M., Monday through Friday, when our offices are open. A member of the team will confirm your price before any work begins.

Pinehollow Outfitters
Everything for the trail, the campsite, and the road.
Welcome to Pinehollow Outfitters, the family-run store where you can find gear for hiking, camping, and outdoor travel of every kind.
Our four floors:
First Floor: Camping gear — tents, sleeping bags, and cooking sets.
Second Floor: Outerwear — jackets, rainwear, and casual clothing.
Third Floor: Footwear — hiking boots, sandals, and socks.
Fourth Floor: Wheeled Gear — bicycles, scooters, and carts.
If you plan to make a special trip in, please call ahead to confirm availability. Please also note that only items from our Outerwear range may be reserved through our website. All other stock must be viewed in the store before purchase.
Open daily from 9:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
----------------------
Free Gear Check-Up Weekend
Saturday and Sunday, November 8 and 9, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
Bring in your bicycle, scooter, or cart for a no-cost inspection and adjustment by our trained staff. Items purchased elsewhere are welcome — you do not need a receipt from our store. Our team will check brakes, wheels, and moving parts, and make small adjustments on the spot.
If a replacement piece is needed, we can place a special order and have it shipped to your home address within two weeks, saving you the trip back.
This year, sessions will take place on the floor directly above our Footwear department.
----------------------
Perfect Stop Before Our Big Group Trip
Reviewer: Karen Sato
I've shopped at Pinehollow Outfitters twice this year and can't say enough good things. Each July I take a group of twelve visitors across the Pinehollow Ridge for five days on foot, and before this summer's trip we all needed matching rain jackets. We had tried three other stores that week without success. The staff here pulled options in every size we needed and let us try them on together. Everyone was outfitted in under an hour. I'll definitely be back next season when we need new boots.
Rating: 5 out of 5

Danforth Property Management, Leasing Division
Bexton House, 22 Sefton Road
Notice of Renewal and Optional Space Offer
Reference: WB-4052
For ground-floor tenants of the Weybridge Building whose agreements end this quarter.
The adjoining suite has become vacant, as its former occupant moved to a larger site, and we are now offering it to current tenants before advertising it. The space is divided into three zones, which are shown in the attached plan.
Tenants may take the space on either of two terms. Under Option A, you would take all three zones for the full three-year term at the reduced rate given in your renewal letter. Under Option B, you would take the whole space for one year with the option to renew, although this option will proceed only if at least four tenants choose it. Under either option, heavy items may not be stored in Zone 3, as its floor cannot hold heavy goods.
Please deliver your written reply by December 5 to this office, which is open on weekdays from nine to five.
Leasing Administrator
----------------------
Weybridge Building adjoining-suite plan (reference WB-4052).
Orientation: the corridor runs along the north side.
Zone 1 — Area: about 40 square meters. Access: direct from the corridor. Partitions: cannot be moved. Services: water connected.
Zone 2 — Area: about 25 square meters. Access: through Zone 1 only. Partitions: can be moved. Services: power only.
Zone 3 — Area: about 15 square meters. Access: from the side passage. Partitions: cannot be moved. Services: none.
Legend: a solid line marks a partition that cannot be moved and a dashed line one that can. Measurements are approximate.
----------------------
From: Bernard Pulaski
To: Gregory Maddox
Copy: Accounts Section
Subject: Reply to Notice WB-4052
Date: November 26
Dear Mr. Maddox,
Thank you for offering the adjoining suite to current tenants. I plan to use Zone 2 as a client reception with its own entrance, and Zone 1 for storing our records.
I am glad to take the space, but I cannot commit the firm for the full three-year term. In addition, I can sign only after our senior partner returns from overseas in January, so I would ask you to confirm that the reception plan can proceed and to allow me more time to sign.
Bernard Pulaski
Office Manager, Trescott Legal Services, Suite 6
P.S. I am reachable at the suite most afternoons.
